messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High error rate for tool/function-calls from tenant hawthorne-health in dedicated pool dp-67 — 15min error rate 14% (ToolCallParseError). Pager routed to eng-oncall.

sarah.oncall: ack — looking now, pulling logs from dp-67

raj.engineer: I see a spike in ToolCallParseError around the 12:23 deploy window. Error text is "Field 'metadata' expected object, got string" for a subset of tool calls.

ana.runtime: pinging routing metadata — this tenant was on the new parser rollout (parser:v2.1.0) in dp-67 about 12:20. We have a canary flag on but looks like some legacy customer payloads hit v2.1 and failed.

mike.ml: can you paste an example payload? trying to repro locally.

hawthorne-sre: FYI our ingestion includes a `metadata` field that is sometimes a string (legacy clients), new schema expects object. We've been aggregating both formats for months. Nothing changed client-side this morning.

raj.engineer: paste from logs:

```json
{
  "tool": "invoice_extractor",
  "metadata": "customer:hawthorne,env:prod",
  "inputs": [...],
  "request_id": "req_0a12b"
}
```

raj.engineer: parser:v2.1 validates metadata as object and throws ToolCallParseError when string provided. That matches.

ana.runtime: impact: ~12% of toolcall traffic from hawthorne is failing with 400/parse errors; remaining calls succeed. Dedicated pool isolation means other tenants unaffected.

julia.support: notified hawthorne support channel, letting them know we're working on mitigation. They reported user-facing errors for their end users.

sarah.oncall: mitigation options: 1) rollback parser rollout for dp-67 -> route tenant back to parser:v2.0; 2) add a compatibility shim in runtime to coerce string->object for `metadata`; 3) route hawthorne toolcalls to fallback node group with v2.0. Prefer fastest that reduces customer impact.

raj.engineer: rollback parser rollout for dp-67 is quickest. I can flip the rollout flag. Suggest also gating any global rollout until we patch parser with backward compatibility.

mike.ml: note: parser v2.1 has other improvements, but we didn't vendor-check for legacy string metadata. We'll add a non-destructive coercion that wraps string into {"raw": "..."}. Patch ETA ~90m.

hana.runtime: sarah, I can apply a temporary router rule to force hawthorne to parser:v2.0 while raj triggers rollback for the dp. That avoids full dp rollback if we prefer.

sarah.oncall: do router rule + patch workflow. hawthorne notified. Raj, can you apply router rule now?

raj.engineer: applying rule:

```bash
# force route for hawthorne-health -> parser:v2.0
routerctl set-route --tenant hawthorne-health --route-key toolcall-parser --value v2.0 --scope dp-67
```

raj.engineer: rule applied. Confirming metrics... error rate dropping (reported 2m after change).

incident-bot: [INFO] Route change detected for tenant hawthorne-health (dp-67) by raj.engineer — reducing traffic to parser:v2.1

hawthorne-sre: seeing immediate improvement — errors down on our side. thanks.

julia.support: updating customer slack: "We're routing your toolcalls to a stable parser and working on a permanent fix. No action required on your side."

mike.ml: starting patch branch to add coercion for metadata string->object. I'll open PR and request an expedited review.

raj.engineer: can we also add a temporary eval rule on the parser to log occurrences with sample request_id for later triage? helps QA verify patch.

ana.runtime: added log sampling at parser ingress for hawthorne-health (rate=1%). config: `parser.log_sample=0.01` for tenant.

sarah.oncall: status update for pager: mitigation in place (router rule), customer impact reduced to <1%. Planned follow-ups: 1) expedited patch and deploy to parser service (Mike + Raj), 2) remove router rule after patch validated, 3) postmortem covering rollout gating and schema compatibility tests.

mike.ml: opened PR #8732 with coercion, tests added (unit + integration), requesting urgent review from eng-runtime.

raj.engineer: patch LGTM from me. planning a staged deploy to dp-67 first, then remove router rule.

hawthorne-sre: we appreciate the quick action. Will hold client-change tickets until you confirm removal of the router rule.

ana.runtime: deploying parser patch to canary nodes in dp-67 now (rolling).

incident-bot: [DEPLOY] parser:v2.1.1 rollout to dp-67 canaries initiated by ana.runtime.

mike.ml: canaries healthy for 10m, sampled logs show metadata coercion applied, no parse errors in samples.

raj.engineer: promoting to full dp-67.

ana.runtime: promoted. monitoring.

raj.engineer: removing router rule now to route hawthorne back to parser:v2.1.1

```bash
routerctl delete-route --tenant hawthorne-health --route-key toolcall-parser --scope dp-67
```

raj.engineer: rule removed. Metrics: stable, error rate holding at baseline (<0.5%).

julia.support: sent customer update: "Patch deployed, we've removed temporary routing. Please report if you see any residual errors."

hawthorne-sre: confirmed no new errors, thanks for the fast turnaround.

sarah.oncall: incident status -> resolved (mitigated + patch deployed). Will file a short postmortem with timeline + action items. Assigning follow-ups: eng-runtime to add schema-compat tests, eng-ml to include legacy payloads in pre-release validation, product to review rollout gating.

mike.ml: noted — I'll add legacy payload corpus to our CI harness.

ana.runtime: will add a rollout checklist item to verify tenant backward-compatibility sampling before enabling new parsers.

incident-bot: [RESOLVED] Incident hawthorne-health: ToolCallParseError spike in dp-67 mitigated at 1738215945.

sarah.oncall: thanks team. handoff to daytime rotation for postmortem write-up.
